'''Adolph Winkler Goodman''' (July 20, 1915 – July 30, 2004) was an American mathematician who contributed to [[number theory]], [[graph theory]] and to the theory of [[univalent functions]]:<ref name="quaternion">See the brief [[#{{harvid|The Editorial Staff|2004}}|obituary on him]] published on the newsletter of the department of Mathematics of the [[University of South Florida]].</ref> [[Goodman's conjecture|The conjecture]] on the coefficients of multivalent functions named after him is considered the most interesting challenge in the area after the [[Bieberbach conjecture]], proved by [[Louis de Branges]] in 1985.<ref name="Haymanxi+162">According to {{harvtxt|Hayman|1994|loc=p. xi and p. 163}}.</ref>

==Life and work ==

In 1948, he made a mathematical conjecture on coefficients of {{math|''ρ''}}-valent functions, first published in his [[Columbia University]] dissertation thesis<ref>{{cite book |title=On some determinants related to {{math|ρ}}-valent formulas |last=Goodman |first=A W |publisher=Columbia University |year=1948 |oclc=36602209 }}.</ref> and then in a closely following paper.<ref>{{cite journal |title=On some determinants related to {{math|''ρ''}}-valent formulas |last=Goodman |first=A. W. |journal=Transactions of the American Mathematical Society  |year=1948 |volume=63 |issue=1 |pages=175–92 |doi=10.1090/S0002-9947-1948-0023910-X |doi-access=free }}</ref> After the proof of the Bieberbach conjecture by Louis de Branges, this conjecture is considered the most interesting challenge in the field,<ref name="Haymanxi+162" /> and he himself and coauthors answered affirmatively to the conjecture for some classes of {{math|''ρ''}}-valent functions.<ref>His contributions are described in the brief survey on [[Goodman's conjecture]] found in {{harv|Hayman|1994|pp=162–163}}.</ref> His researches in the field continued in the paper ''Univalent functions and nonanalytic curves'', published in 1957:<ref>{{cite journal |title=Univalent functions and nonanalytic curves |last=Goodman |first=A. W. |journal=Proceedings of the American Mathematical Society |year=1957 |volume= 8 |issue= 3 |pages= 598–601 |doi = 10.1090/S0002-9939-1957-0086879-9 |doi-access=free }}</ref> in 1968, he published the survey ''Open problems on univalent and multivalent functions'',<ref>{{cite journal |title=Open problems on Univalent and multivalent functions |last=Goodman |first=A. W. |journal=  Bulletin of the American Mathematical Society|year= 1968 |volume=74 |issue=6 |pages=1035–1051 |doi=10.1090/S0002-9904-1968-12045-2 |doi-access=free }}</ref> which eventually led him to write the two-volume book ''Univalent Functions''.<ref>{{cite book
  |title=Univalent functions
  |author=Goodman, A. W.
  |volume= 1
  |isbn=9780936166100
  |lccn=83007930
  |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=PC7vAAAAMAAJ
  |year=1983
  |publisher=Mariner Pub. Co.
}}</ref><ref>{{cite book
  |title=Univalent functions
  |author=Goodman, A.W.
  |volume= 2
  |isbn=9780936166117
  |lccn=83007930
  |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=wi
  |year=1983
  |publisher=Mariner Pub. Co.
}}</ref>

Apart from his research activity, He was actively involved in teaching: he wrote several college and high school textbooks including ''Analytic Geometry and the Calculus'', and the five-volume set ''Algebra from A to Z''.<ref name="quaternion"/>

He retired in 1993, became a Distinguished Professor Emeritus in 1995, and died in 2004.<ref name="quaternion"/>
